- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 74.23 → 75.99 in Example 1), then corrects downward — model lags in recognizing peak decay.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds high forecasts longer than observed price corrections.
- Forecast tends to be too optimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually adjusts — but often adjusts too late or too much.
- Model underestimates downward trends in late history (e.g., 74.23 → 69.36 in Example 4), suggesting it fails to recognize sustained decline.
- High forecast variance in early days correlates with low true price variance — model overreacts to short-term noise.
- Model fails to capture “recovery” patterns after sharp drops — e.g., 70.42 → 72.66 in Example 1, model doesn’t anticipate rebound.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are too bullish in early periods, then too bearish in late periods — model exhibits “inverted” bias over time.
